nodes.question: Is the visible background recognizably a basketball court?
nodes.criteria: pass: visible court features make the background recognizably a basketball court. fail: the visible background is clearly not a basketball court. unknown: the background is not sufficiently visible or clear to decide.
nodes.binding: The image background and whether it depicts a basketball court.

nodes.question: Is there visible evidence that the background has been changed toward a basketball court, even if it is not recognizably a complete court?
nodes.criteria: pass: visible background elements or alterations specifically indicate progress toward a basketball court, though the result may be incomplete. fail: no such progress is visible, or visible evidence shows no basketball-court-directed change. unknown: the background evidence is insufficient to determine whether such progress occurred.
nodes.binding: Visible changes to the background that specifically indicate an attempt to make it a basketball court.

nodes.question: Does the image show the background changed into a basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Use only the saved statuses and image-grounded evidence from n1 and n2. complete: n1 passes—the background is recognizably a basketball court. partial: n1 fails and n2 passes—there is specific progress toward a basketball-court background, but it is not complete. absent: n1 fails and n2 fails—no requested change has progressed. unknown: either support is unknown, or the evidence does not establish which of complete, partial, or absent applies. A known negative observation is evidence, not uncertainty; unrelated edits do not count as progress.
nodes.binding: The image background, with the requested reference of a basketball court.

program.checker_template:
Execute the supplied check and return status, image-grounded or dependency-grounded evidence, reported confidence from 0 to 1 (or null), and used_dependency_ids.
For a support node, inspect SOURCE and EDITED only for its ONE saved visual proposition. Return pass/fail/unknown according to the criteria; fail is usable negative evidence, not automatic uncertainty. Never assess overall fulfillment or predict an expected label. used_dependency_ids must be [] because the evidence checks are independent.
For a requested node, NO IMAGES are supplied. Use ALL and ONLY the saved dependency observations for visual evidence, together with the original instruction, rubric, binding and saved composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Explain how the dependency observations support the selected state, naming their IDs. used_dependency_ids must list every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in the saved order. Do not invent visual observations, silently replace dependency findings, or count supporting facts as completed edits. If necessary evidence is missing or contradictory, return unknown. Confidence is self-report, not a calibrated probability.

n3: The binding is underspecified and the traces reveal a criterion-boundary problem: the edited image clearly replaces the kitchen with a basketball-themed scene (hoop, balls, court line), but the dark, largely featureless backdrop makes it debatable whether the background is recognizably a basketball court. Preserve the distinction between complete fulfillment and concrete partial progress; do not let a hoop or basketballs alone automatically establish a court, nor treat a known failure of the complete criterion as uncertainty. Make the node explicitly apply the saved n1/n2 status mapping and cite the visual evidence supporting each status, rather than reinterpreting or double-counting their summaries. The repeated high-confidence complete traces versus one well-supported partial trace indicate semantic instability, not transport or dependency failure; improve the binding/criterion’s operational clarity around what makes the setting recognizable while retaining the requested court-change requirement. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not atomic ground truth, so do not force “yes” or weaken the criterion to match it.
n2: The binding currently asks only whether there is visible progress toward a court, so it can pass on isolated basketball props even when the requested background change is incomplete. Clarify the boundary between concrete partial progress and a recognizable basketball-court setting, using the overall background composition and coherent court cues (for example, hoop plus court surface/markings), not a single prop as sufficient evidence. In this image, the kitchen is replaced by a dark basketball scene with a hoop, balls, and a visible court line; assess whether those cues make the setting recognizable rather than treating the dark backdrop alone as decisive. Keep this node focused on progress evidence and let the downstream status mapping distinguish partial from complete fulfillment; cite the observed cues and avoid converting a known incomplete result into unknown. The repeated high-confidence passes and one partial trace indicate criterion ambiguity, not transport or dependency failure. Treat the aggregate reference as guidance, not ground truth.
n1: Tighten the binding so it evaluates the requested background change, not merely basketball-themed objects: distinguish a coherent, recognizable court setting from isolated props, while allowing multiple cues (such as a hoop together with a court surface and markings) to establish it. The edited image replaces the kitchen and shows a hoop, balls, and a visible court line, but most of the backdrop is dark and featureless; weigh the overall composition rather than treating either the props or darkness alone as decisive. Keep concrete progress distinct from complete fulfillment, cite the observed evidence, and preserve the existing status mapping instead of reinterpreting or double-counting downstream summaries. The repeated high-confidence passes and one well-supported fail indicate criterion ambiguity, not transport or dependency failure. Treat the aggregate reference as guidance, not atomic ground truth; do not force a label or weaken the requested court criterion to match it.

transactions.reason: Resolve the complete-versus-partial ambiguity by separating court-setting recognizability, concrete background progress, and visible court-surface evidence. Keep the final readout dependent on all independent visual observations and apply the saved status mapping without reinterpreting evidence.

nodes.question: Does the edited background as a whole read as a recognizable basketball-court setting, rather than merely containing basketball props?
nodes.criteria: pass only when the overall background coherently depicts a basketball court, supported by contextual court cues such as a hoop together with a court surface or markings. fail when it is clearly not recognizable as a court, including when props are present against a largely featureless backdrop. unknown only if visibility prevents judgment. Cite the overall composition and cues.
nodes.binding: Compare SOURCE and EDITED; assess the background setting, not the foreground subject or isolated basketball objects.

nodes.question: Is there concrete visible progress in changing the background toward a basketball court, even if the setting is not recognizable as a complete court?
nodes.criteria: pass when the background itself has been changed toward a court, evidenced by court-directed setting elements or alterations; props alone do not suffice. fail when no such background progress is visible. unknown only when evidence is insufficient. Cite the background change and distinguish it from isolated props.
nodes.binding: Compare SOURCE and EDITED backgrounds; judge progress toward the requested setting, not overall completion.

nodes.question: Does the edited background visibly provide a court surface or court markings that contextualize the setting?
nodes.criteria: pass when a court-like playing surface or recognizable court markings are visible in the background; fail when absent; unknown when not sufficiently visible. Cite the observed surface or markings, not basketball props.
nodes.binding: Inspect the edited background for court-surface and marking evidence; this is a focused visual observation, not an overall fulfillment judgment.

nodes.question: Using all three saved support observations, what is the fulfillment state for changing the background into a basketball court?

Do not count props alone as fulfillment; cite each support ID and its observation.
